title: Affected-only test selection in the inner loop
measured: Status: rejected. The Proof is already one named test file, and land gates are cached or skipped when slow. Evidence: unmeasured.

threshold: pooled net at least 1.0% of run cost with the CI lower bound above 0

Residual gross saving is 0.024% of run [0.012, 0.038] and net is -0.020% [-0.033, -0.009] once the report write and the lead's read are charged (n=260 runs); the all-notification ceiling is 0.54% gross, -0.19% net. $0 spent. Evidence: [2026-10-20-verdict-line-returns.md](results/2026-10-20-verdict-line-returns.md).

The avoidable tail after the first green Proof is 13.37% of build-task cost [12.52, 14.26] (n=2919 transcripts, 2320 with a green Proof), but 21.2% of the tail is fixes [19.7, 22.7] against a 20% limit and 25.6% of tasks edit after green; `agents/build-task.md` already says "Stop at green". $0 spent of $4.75. Evidence: [2026-10-20-build-task-stop-at-green.md](results/2026-10-20-build-task-stop-at-green.md).

title: Build-task tests every boundary a `Data:` line implies
mechanism: (`agents/build-task.md` line telling the builder to test each limit the task's `Data:` line names, aimed at the review repair loop on `src/truncate.js` `max < 3`).
measured: Status: rejected, no wall gain at n=15. Wall -5.6 s (-2.9% mean, CI [-31.7, +17.7] s, exact MW p=0.645; one edge cell hung after finishing, its wall corrected from the transcript), cost +1.0% (CI [-0.045, +0.055] $, p=0.81), hidden 255/255 in both arms. Fix-review loops 3 of 15 in both arms, and all three edge loops still concern `max < 3`, so the line did not stop the loop. Evidence: [2026-10-19-speed-round7.md](results/2026-10-19-speed-round7.md).
retryWhen: a run log shows the builder skipping a boundary its `Data:` line names; the prompt change is in [2026-10-19-speed-round7.md](results/2026-10-19-speed-round7.md). Cause: the fixture plan left `max < 3` undefined (builder and reviewer disagreed), and the hidden tests stopped at max 3; the follow-up fixture fix defines `truncate` as throwing a `RangeError` below 3, so later loop rates are not comparable.

title: Builder lands its own task
mechanism: (the build-task builder runs the landing itself, so the run-unit spends no land turn and no readback turn).
metric: Refusals after a green builder check; run-unit cost in land and readback turns
threshold: 0 refusals after green, and CI lower bound at least 3% of run-unit cost
measured: Status: rejected on the quality guard. 34 of 267 run-unit land calls (233 landed) are refused after a green builder `--check` of the same task, 0 required; landing catches Land gate, red-proof and Data: failures the builder check does not. Land plus readback requests are 14.9% of run-unit cost, CI [11.8, 17.6], so the bound clears 3% but the guard stops it. $0 spent. Evidence: [2026-10-20-builder-lands-own-task.md](results/2026-10-20-builder-lands-own-task.md).
retryWhen: the builder check runs every check the landing runs (Land gate, red-proof, Data:) so refusals after a green check reach 0.

title: Cache TTL of 1 hour on `build-task`, `review-branch` and `fix-review`
mechanism: (`subagentPromptCacheTtl` or per-agent `experimental: { cacheTtl: 1h }`, now set only on `run-unit`).
measured: Status: rejected. On real-use transcripts 1h would raise cache spend: build-task -33.0% [-34.4, -31.5] (n=2919), review-branch -43.8% [-44.9, -42.8] (n=444), fix-review -41.4% [-43.3, -39.7] (n=123); negative means 1h costs more, since few gaps pass 300 s. Evidence: [2026-10-20-cache-ttl-real-use.md](results/2026-10-20-cache-ttl-real-use.md).
retryWhen: these agents start idling over 5 minutes between requests, such as long proof waits.

title: Cache warm-up stagger before fan-out
measured: Status: rejected. It is harness-level, `run-unit` already uses a 1-hour cache TTL, and the gain is cost, not wall time. Evidence: unmeasured.
retryWhen: the harness exposes a measured wall-time effect of cache warm-up.

title: Compact build tasks at medium effort as speed-pass Task 6
mechanism: (`perf(agents): run compact build tasks at medium effort`, reverted in `f21c4311`).
measured: Status: rejected. The branch arm carrying it had a 315.2 s median wall against 189.9 s for main, and the repaired arm without it was still 28% above main; n=3, so the gap is within noise. Evidence: [2026-10-02-speed.md](results/2026-10-02-speed.md).
retryWhen: a larger run-to-run sample or a pressure cell shows the lower effort keeps the pass rate and cuts wall time (`build-task` at `medium` later landed on pass rate and cost alone, see the pointers below).

metric: USD per cell vs main, n=5 x 5 tasks, sonnet
threshold: at least 3% under main

retryWhen: a later change makes the split the only remaining text cost, or a same-batch test shows at least 3% under main.

title: Dedupe repeat Read of an unchanged range
mechanism: A repeat Read of an unchanged file range returns a short stub (PreToolUse hook on Read, or one prompt line in `review-branch-deep` and `solve-hard`).
measured: Status: rejected. 0 qualifying repeats in review-branch-deep and solve-hard (280 agents, $168): saving 0.00%, 95% CI [0.00, 0.00], bar 3%. Across all agent types 26 repeats in 5,980 agents, about $0.10. Evidence: [2026-10-20-repeat-read.md](results/2026-10-20-repeat-read.md).
retryWhen: exact unchanged re-reads show up in real-use transcripts.

mechanism: Move the delegation rules out of the session text into hook text delivered at the first Agent call.
metric: USD per cell and hidden tests, n=5 x 5 tasks, sonnet
threshold: lower first-call cache write with no change in delegation

title: Done-rule lines: each variant took effect, each warning kind in full output
mechanism: Done rules that ask for output showing each order, seed, timezone or input variant took effect, and each warning kind and README rule for touched code read in full.
metric: USD per cell and hidden tests, n=5 x 5 tasks, sonnet
threshold: cost per cell no higher than round 1 ($0.1203)
measured: Status: rejected as worded; round 3 keeps a bounded form. Measured through the round 2 bundle: shuffle and rotation loops on test-pollution rose from 1.6 to 4.2 per cell, calls from 5.2 to 11.0, tool output by 5.6 KB per cell and README reads from 1.1 to 1.7. Cost about +$0.025 for loops and proofs and +$0.009 for tool output. It bought the first test-pollution passes by any arm (2/5), but most of the spend went into loops that ended in a fail.
retryWhen: never as an unbounded proof rule; see the round 3 entry.

title: Event-driven wait instead of the 5 s `wait-report` poll
measured: Status: rejected. The mean latency is 2.5 s per slot, and a hook would add overhead to every session. Evidence: unmeasured.
retryWhen: the poll shows up as a measured share of a build's wall time.

title: Fast mode for the serial hard unit
measured: Status: rejected. It raises cost for a wall-time gain. Evidence: unmeasured.
retryWhen: pricing makes fast mode cost-neutral.

title: find-open-points agent at low effort
mechanism: (a new `open-points` kind in the effort table runs the open-point agent at `low` effort).
metric: Saving, % of the find-open-points bucket
threshold: at least 3% of the bucket
measured: Status: rejected, structurally unreachable. Of 79 real-use runs ($20.76) only the 34 medium-effort runs (11.4% of the bucket) can change; 80% of the bucket runs xhigh or max because `raised()` in `hooks/agent-effort.mjs` (323b1ab8) lifts the agent to the session effort before the kind table is read. Hidden thinking in the reachable runs is $0.43 (2.1%; 4.2% with 14 runs of unrecorded effort), so even removing all of it misses 3%; a 30-50% cut gives 0.6-1.0%. $0 spent, no paid run. Evidence: [2026-10-20-fop-effort-low.md](results/2026-10-20-fop-effort-low.md).
retryWhen: the xhigh/max raise is dropped or lowered for the open-point agent (a separate idea, fop-no-raise, with a recall guard and a paid A/B of at least 8 brief pairs), or most runs start at medium.

title: Fix the model that reaches build-task (tier leak)
mechanism: (find why non-exo build-tasks bill Opus when the tier table says Sonnet, then fix the cause: the `run-unit` brief or `agent-effort.mjs` keeping a dispatch-named model).
metric: Saving, % of the billed-Opus build-task bucket
threshold: lower bound at least 3% of the Opus bucket (about $1.1) over at least 8 sessions
measured: Status: rejected. The premise was a counting artifact: the advisor tool entry in each transcript's `api-request-shape` line names `claude-opus-5-5` and was never called, so a first-model grep counted 214 of 225 non-exo build-tasks as Opus while 221 billed Sonnet. The real leak is 4 build-tasks in 1 session, $2.35: the `run-unit` copied the lead's `exo:solve-hard: model opus, effort high.` line onto `exo:build-task`, and `agent-effort.mjs` keeps a dispatch-named model. That is under the 8-session floor and about $0.6 as a point estimate, below the $1.1 bar (n=225 build-tasks, 916 agents scanned). A one-line fix in `agents/run-unit.md` (pass `model` and `effort` only to `exo:solve-hard`) is unbuilt. $0 spent. Evidence: [2026-10-20-build-task-tier-leak.md](results/2026-10-20-build-task-tier-leak.md).
retryWhen: a model-mix scan that reads the billed model from assistant `message.model` shows build-tasks billed above the table in at least 8 sessions.

title: Fix the usage and error text of exo's scripts from run-log error counts
mechanism: (mine run logs for retries and invalid-argument errors on `next-task`, `land-task`, `land-slot`, `wait-report` and `verify`; rewrite the text they hit, or add a check that fails on a new error without a hint; one-time, not a new agent stage).
measured: Status: rejected. Over 1,198 non-sweep run sessions ($3,387), all exo-script retry events together are 1,694 events, $50.5 = 1.49% of run cost; the best script, land-task.mjs, has 0.264 events per run and 0.165% of cost, against a bar of 0.5 per run or 2%. Most events are permission or hook text and real state failures. Evidence: [2026-10-20-script-retries.md](results/2026-10-20-script-retries.md).
retryWhen: one script shows 0.5 or more retry events per run, or 2% of run cost, from its own usage or error text.

title: Fold plain-Bash phase chains into exo script output
mechanism: (recurring chains of 3+ plain-Bash lead requests in one exo phase, such as code reads, git housekeeping and log reads, print as one script output).
metric: Saving, % of run cost
threshold: raw fold saving at least 3% of run for the chosen class, and saving times scriptable fraction at least 1.5% of run
measured: Status: rejected. The lead reads code in `read` chains worth a raw fold saving of 2.73% of run [2.23, 3.45] (n=261 runs), but 0 of 20 sampled chains (0 of 232) match a command template seen in 5 or more runs, so scriptable saving is 0%; recipe-like chains (git housekeeping 0.01%, git-inspect 0.16%, exo artifacts 0.11%) are far under the 1.5% bar. $0 spent. Evidence: [2026-10-20-fold-plain-bash-chains.md](results/2026-10-20-fold-plain-bash-chains.md).
retryWhen: a measured set of plain-Bash chains recurs as the same command template in 5 or more runs and holds at least 1.5% of run cost, or a cheaper helper (`exo:locate-code` or a Sonnet reader) takes the lead's exploratory code reading, which changes who reads and needs its own test with a quality guard on decisions.

title: Fork dispatch for wave siblings
mechanism: (after the lead reads the brief and rules once, spawn wave `build-task`s as forks that inherit the lead's cached conversation instead of fresh agents that re-read them).
measured: Status: untried. It could skip 2-3 read turns per task and a cold cache write, but cost is uncertain (the fork carries the lead's context), and it breaks the clean-room `build-task` design with lead bias. Nearest entry: "The dispatch carries the read set", which inlines text; a fork shares the cache instead. No Anthropic-engineer talk transcript was found; the only talk summary read is third-party ([dev.to](https://dev.to/kazuya_dev/aws-reinvent-2025-what-anthropic-learned-building-ai-agents-in-2025-aim277-16lc)) and it says sub-agents "didn't parallelize well in practice", so the claim below rests on docs and blog posts, not a talk. Evidence: unmeasured, confidence low (one first-party source): [SDK subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents) (a fork inherits the parent conversation; a non-fork gets only the prompt string).
retryWhen: a run shows the brief and rules reads as a measured share of build-task wall time and a fork keeps the pass rate on a pressure cell.

title: Haiku for `run-unit`
measured: Status: rejected. Routing risk is too high for an unmeasured gain; effort was tested first. Evidence: unmeasured.
retryWhen: `run-unit` at `low` effort holds its routing pressure cases and a cheaper tier still looks needed.

title: Hot-file index for locate-code and find-open-points
mechanism: (an index of files read by at least 3 other sessions replaces whole-file Reads by cited ranges plus a pointer).
metric: Saving, % of the two agents' cost
threshold: bootstrap 95% CI lower bound at least 3% of the bucket
measured: Status: rejected. Replayed saving 2.78% of the $28.84 bucket, CI [1.33, 4.52] (98 sessions, 98 replaced reads); about 0.2% of a run. Whole-file Reads of hot files carry only $1.35, not the $2.79 of the gate, so the bar needs a 64% cut of it; the replay cuts 59%. Quality guard passed (0 of 1058 cited lines outside the kept ranges). Index build and read cost not charged. $0 spent. Evidence: [2026-10-20-hot-file-index.md](results/2026-10-20-hot-file-index.md).
retryWhen: whole-file Reads of hot files carry more than $2.00 of a bucket of at most $29, or the two agents grow past 5% of a run.

title: Invariant-edge Red: a `Data:` quantifier ("exactly", "at most", "never") needs a Red test at inputs 0, 1 and below any constant
mechanism: (`test-design.md` rule, optionally a `land-task.mjs checkTask` guard).
measured: Status: untried. It removes the review, fix, probe and re-review loop when it fires (about 25 s per run on average, 2 of 6 runs), but it can over-test trivial tasks. Evidence: unmeasured (transcript estimate).
retryWhen: a run again shows a reviewer finding a defect at an edge input that the plan's `Data:` states.

title: Three isolated review judges replace the single review-branch pass
mechanism: Three sessions per case, each with a verbatim slice of review-branch (plan fit, code standard, weakened tests), merged with merge-reviews.
metric: Seeds hit and false alarms on the 10 pilot cases, tokens per case
threshold: Pilot: no lost safe seed and under 2 added false alarms on 4 controls. Full run: at least 2 more std/weakened seeds than control, no rise in false alarms, tokens at most 2x control unless a catch is added.
measured: Pilot passed its stop rule at a ceiling. Seeds hit 15/15 vs control 14/15; green-first 3/3 both; control false alarms 3 vs 1 (all sql-user db.js:10-12, one cell counted twice for two judges). Tokens 3,264,369 vs 1,168,767 (2.79x), cost $13.77 vs $5.01 (2.75x); wall max 29.3 s vs 29.2 s, wall sum 71.9 s. Ceiling: the pilot cannot show a gain. Full run not run; the token ratio already exceeds the 2x bar. Evidence: [2026-10-22-review-judges-pilot.md](results/2026-10-22-review-judges-pilot.md).
retryWhen: the std-* and weak-* seeded fixtures exist, so a full run can show a catch gain over the single reviewer.

title: L1.1 Protected-token conservation check
mechanism: multiset diff of backticks, numbers and boundary words per instruction diff in `npm run check`; fails `LOST` unless `Accept-cut:`.
threshold: recall >= 50% AND median <= 2 flags on never-restored trim commits.
measured: recall 38/61 = 62.3%; median 0 flags on 18 trim commits (only 18 exist, not 20; mean 1.1, max 5). n = 61 restores. Cost: $0. Verdict: PASS as written, impact small. Incremental over the landed `verify/checks/boundary-words.mjs` is 3/61 = 5% of restores. The test is circular (the cutter is found as the commit that removed the token). 59% of instruction-file commits (657/1121) would carry a LOST flag, which is friction the n = 18 sample hides.

title: L1.2 Restore-to-pin memory
mechanism: hash lines deleted then re-added in history; a later diff deleting a pinned line prints `PINNED`.
threshold: >= 10 would-block events AND precision >= 60%.
measured: 54 pins, 27 events in 19 commits; precision 2/27 = 7.4% exact, 22.2% fuzzy (Jaccard >= 0.8). Variant "any re-add pins": 194 events, 10.8% exact. Cost: $0. Verdict: FAIL. Over 90% of blocks would hit deliberate later cuts. The overlap check recommends merging it into L1.1 and dropping it.

title: L1.3 Edit-survival score
mechanism: share of exo-made added lines surviving 14 days via git blame; ranks files for the next experiment.
threshold: top-vs-bottom quartile spread >= 20 pts AND Spearman rho >= 0.4 against next-2-week fix commits.
measured: n = 174 files, 10598 lines; survival 79.5%, spread 72.4 pts (bottom 26.6%, top 99.0%); rho = 0.387 (min-lines 5 / 20: 0.346 / 0.347); control rho 0.116. Cost: $0. Verdict: FAIL (rho 0.387 < 0.4). The test leaks, so 0.387 is inflated; the leak-free variant leaves rho undefined. "Any change" survival is 34.1%, which the idea does not distinguish from the stated reading.

title: L2.1 Recurrence alarm
mechanism: parse review findings and run.log into findings.jsonl; print `RECURRING <class>` when no check covers a class.
threshold: (a) unmapped share of second-half findings <= 15%; (b) alarm precision >= 70%; (c) Red alarm >= 4 days before a83d9a04.
measured: (a) 27/158 = 17.1% (fail); (b) 10/10 alarms but non-discriminating; (c) alarm 6.2 days early (pass). n = 158 findings, 72 runs. Cost: $0. Verdict: FAIL on (a). The alias map was built on all data, so (a) is optimistic. Estimated gain about 14 min over 72 runs, and only if the user then writes the check.

title: L2.2 Learned co-change rule
mechanism: plan-check warns "B usually changes with A" from git co-change plus block-reason files.
threshold: recall >= 5/8 blocked "missing from the file list" tasks; <= 1 warning per 5 tasks on 40 landed tasks.
measured: recall 0/7 (only 7 distinct blocks; original plans are gitignored, so an approximation was used); 4.1 warnings per 5 tasks (13 of 40 tasks warned, mostly release-file noise). n = 7 and 40. Cost: $0. Verdict: FAIL, both thresholds by a wide margin. Impact 0 repair sessions saved.

title: L2.3 Failure cause field
mechanism: run-plan writes the full `cause:` to state.json and run.log; check fails on a refusal without reason.
threshold: (i) >= 50% of 22 `Full output` paths gone; (ii) >= 4/5 replayed failed sessions get a cause a reader agrees with.
measured: (i) 22/22 gone (pass); (ii) not runnable, no extractor and the failed sessions are deleted. n = 22. Cost: $0. Verdict: INCONCLUSIVE. Commit 6ffbf565 already fixed the placeholder; about 3 of 4 later failures still lack a cause (n = 4). Enabler only; 0 min direct gain.

title: L3.1 Stage checkpoint fork
mechanism: snapshot baseline cells per stage; run the candidate only from the earliest stage it can change.
metric: verify-block weighted tokens (input plus output), verify-only fork vs full flow-unit cell
threshold: Pre-set before spend: (a) verify cost, (b) verify tokens, (c) fix-loop rate, (d) hidden-test pass, (e) cost per sample ratio; (b) tests fork vs full with Mann-Whitney, fail at p < 0.05.
measured: Status: rejected, FAIL on (b). Verify tokens mean 69,943 (sd 6,224) full n=5 vs 86,038 (sd 8,686) fork n=8, Mann-Whitney p=0.008; verify cost $0.222 vs $0.266 (p=0.242), wall 54 s vs 65 s (p=0.380). Fix-loop rate 0/5 vs 0/8 and hidden-test pass 5/5 vs 8/8 carry no information. A fork costs 44% of a full cell ($0.266 vs $0.609). Gap is in the lead (MW p=0.003, cache writes about 8k full vs 16.6k-21.6k fork); subagent tokens match (p=0.661). Evidence: [2026-10-20-checkpoint-fork.md](results/2026-10-20-checkpoint-fork.md).
retryWhen: the comparison excludes cache-creation tokens as a pre-set criterion, or forks share a warm prompt cache with the full cell. Cause: a fresh `claude -p` fork lead pays prompt-cache creation for system prompt, tools and skill load that a full cell lead already has cached, so lead-side measures are biased and more forks would not remove it; restricting the metric to subagents (review-branch, fix-review) is untested.

title: L3.2 Time-paired blocks plus group-sequential stop
mechanism: paired diffs, O'Brien-Fleming looks, futility stop in statistics.mjs.
threshold: (a) paired-slot residual r >= 0.3; (b) mean runs per arm <= 10, verdict equals fixed n = 15 in every round, A/A false stops <= 5%.
measured: (a) pooled r = 0.06 (permutation p = 0.25, n = 50 cells); (b) mean 12.7 runs per arm, verdict match 31-100% (3 of 7 datasets under 95%), A/A false stops 9-19% as written, 1-4% t-corrected but 13.5 runs and 2 mismatches. n = 7 datasets x 1000 orderings. Cost: $0. Verdict: FAIL. The test used z bounds on a t statistic; the corrected variant still fails. Gain about 10-15% fewer runs, not 30-45%.

title: L3.3 Content-keyed baseline pool
mechanism: reuse base cells keyed by hash of loaded files for cost, token and quality; run the candidate arm only.
threshold: >= 80% of key-matched base-arm pairs have p > 0.05 on cost and tokens (Mann-Whitney); wall expected to fail as control.
measured: Replay with the shipped key (`node benchmarks/baseline-pool.mjs replay`): 3/3 matched pairs (100%), cost shifts -2..+5%; wall control p < 0.05 in 1 of 3 (detects drift); pairs of rounds 2-6 with rounds 7-8 shift cost -7..-14%. n = 3 pairs. Cost: $0. Verdict: PASS. Saves about $4.5 per round for cost, token and quality questions, nothing for wall. Pairs are not independent and n = 15 detects only about 10% shifts.

title: L4.1 Structured ledger with duplicate gate
mechanism: JSONL records plus a `--near` Jaccard check that fails a new record close to a rej/nog.
threshold: recall@3 >= 4/5 on cross-linked pairs AND <= 15 of 990 pairs >= tau 0.35; second pass >= 70% rank-1.
measured: recall@3 3/5; 45 of 990 pairs >= tau; max 2-gram Jaccard 0.132, so tau is unreachable. Second pass 13/14 = 93% but leaky. n = 45 records. Cost: $0. Verdict: FAIL. Corrected gate is rank-based (nearest rej/nog top-1 AND same component|lever key). Saving of about $2 per brainstorm round comes from `--near` as a lookup, not from tau.

title: L4.2 Experiment queue ranked by power
mechanism: `--next` sorts un ideas by shrunk estimate over test cost using mde.mjs.
threshold: flags >= 3 of the 4 non-significant rounds (2, 3, 4, 7) as sub-MDE and 0 of round 6.
measured: rounds 2, 3 flagged; 4 and 7 have no recorded estimate; round 6 flagged (its -22% gain was partly a fix-loop imbalance, stage-matched -5.6%). MDE about 80 s at n = 5, 46 s at n = 15. Cost: $0. Verdict: FAIL as written (round 6 flagged). `mde.mjs` takes a pass rate, not seconds. Estimated saving about $54 over 6 rounds if sub-MDE rounds were bundled.

title: L4.3 Retry triggers as dependency graph
mechanism: machine-checkable "Retry when" predicates over metrics and landed changes.
threshold: >= 40% of 45 `Retry when:` lines encode as `after:` or `metric:` over existing fields; `--reopen` prints fan-out dependents.
measured: 15/45 = 33% (58% if not-yet-existing fields count); 19 are external. `--reopen` would give "measured: yes, landed: no", not a clean reopen. n = 45. Cost: $0. Verdict: FAIL (33% < 40%, marginal). Estimated 0-1 reopenings per month. Storage recommendation (JSONL plus generated markdown) had no threshold and was not scored.

title: L5.1 Runtime context ledger plus residency ratchet
mechanism: token-turns by class from transcripts, run-report line, ratchet fails on exo-authored growth over 10%.
threshold: (a) two runs byte-identical; (b) class shares sum to 100 +/- 1%; (c) exo-authored share of flow-unit build-task within +/-5 points of the 10% corpus figure.
measured: (a) pass; (b) pass but vacuous; (c) 38.3% (corpus 19.0%, not 10%). n = 107 flow-unit transcripts, 2684 corpus files. Cost: $0. Verdict: FAIL on (c). Flow-unit is exo-dominated (78% of lead residency), so the "trimming wins at most 10%" claim does not hold for that arm. Supports a ledger, not the 10% premise. No direct token or wall gain.

title: L5.2 Cost-ranked self-pruning of hot rules
mechanism: rank rules by reads x tokens, probe the top-K with the cut-rules harness, per-rule counters.
threshold: >= 3 of 10 top-cost non-boundary rules show no behaviour change in 5/5 probes, together >= 15% of their file's tokens.
measured: 4 rules unchanged at 5/5 (all in lean.md), 33% of lean.md (7% pooled across three files). n = 100 probes. Cost: $1.08 (cap $6). Verdict: PASS on the pre-set threshold, not a basis for cutting those rules. The probes are single-turn and tool-less, so the split is generic best-practice versus repo-fact rules, and the probes were not blind. Saving at most about 130k loaded tokens per 14 days, under 1% of residency.

title: L6.1 Risk-routed first attempt
mechanism: per-task failure-risk prior from past runs; upgrade the top quartile to a higher tier via `riskPin`.
threshold: held-out share of first-attempt failures in the top-25% risk bucket >= 50% and lift >= 2.0.
measured: 5/8 = 62%, lift 2.48 (5-95% bootstrap 0.14-1.00). The file prior adds nothing; file count alone gives 7/8 = 88%. Held-out failure rate fell to 7.2% from 27.7%. n = 262 train, 111 held-out tasks, 8 failures. Cost: $0; paid Test B not run. Verdict: PASS as written with very low power. Test B INCONCLUSIVE (regression to the mean breaks "old pin <= 1/4"; `exo run` refuses inside Claude Code). Gain about 2% of tasks. Worth a paid test only if the failure rate returns to about 25%.

title: L6.2 Adaptive slot count per plan
mechanism: slots = min(DAG width, k) with k from recorded gate time and cores.
threshold: wall -15% or better on >= 60% of wide plans, no plan > 5% slower.
measured: 30 wide plans. No contention, k = 6 or 8: 17/30 = 57%, 0 slower, median -16.5%. With contention (stretch 0.34 per extra task) k = 6: 2/30, k = 8: 8/30, 3 slower. n = 30 plans. Cost: $0. Verdict: FAIL, even the contention-free best case misses 60%. Gain about 1-3% of overall build wall. The contention figure is one implied scalar; per-gate timings at 2, 4 and 6 concurrent slots would fix that.

title: `land-slot`: land one slot in one script call
measured: Status: landed-but-no-gain. Run-unit calls fell 15% (15.3 to 13.0) but total wall, cost and tokens show no effect n=3 can support. Evidence: [2026-10-19-build-speed-rerun.md](results/2026-10-19-build-speed-rerun.md).

title: Land-task refusals in one call
mechanism: (`land-task.mjs --check` runs the report, lint and code-rule checks and prints every refusal in one result, not the first one).
metric: Saving, % of the request cost of build-task turns that call land-task
threshold: at least 3% with a CI lower bound above 3%
measured: Status: rejected. Replay of 50 real-use sessions (508 build-tasks, bucket $14.86): 45 avoidable refusal pairs (44 report then code-rules) save 2.88% of the bucket [1.35, 3.92], 0.10% of run; the upper-bound replay is 4.86% [2.36, 6.75]. Both lower bounds are under 3%. $0 spent. Evidence: [2026-10-20-refusals-in-one-call.md](results/2026-10-20-refusals-in-one-call.md).
retryWhen: a cheaper variant (the report check also reads the code rules in the same call, only for `--check`) is preregistered against a bucket where the saving can reach 3%, or report-format refusals grow past 277 in 508 tasks.

title: Latency-normalized wall as a secondary A/B metric
mechanism: (sum of the predicted latency of the critical-path turns, from a per-model OLS fit of output and cache tokens).
measured: Status: untried as a standing method; used once, as a secondary metric, in round 6. API latency is about 84% of within-class wall variance (stalls about 25%, diffuse per-run speed about 59%), and normalizing strips it: round 6 stage-matched, wall -5.6% (p=0.52) against latency-normalized wall -21.0 s (-10.6%, p=0.0012); all runs, normalized wall sd 17.7 to 53.7 s against raw 28.1 to 66.5 s. A 10 s effect is under the 38 s within-class sd, so raw wall needs far more than n=15. Risk: the fit is per model and per round, and it counts turns and tokens only, so it cannot see a change that makes the API slower per token. Evidence: [round 6](results/2026-10-19-speed-round6.md).
retryWhen: the next speed A/B, report it beside raw wall and the stage-matched result.

mechanism: (raise `BLOCK_TASK_LIMIT` in `nextBlock` from 8 to 12 or 16 so the lead sends fewer `exo:run-unit` blocks, which removes next-task, dispatch and wake cycles and run-unit startups).
metric: Net saving, % of run cost
threshold: at least 0.24% of run with a CI lower bound above 0, and at least 1% of run at the best cap

Replay of the real `nextBlock` on 24 post-10-09 sessions removes 3 of 31 blocks: net saving 0.32-0.42% of run (CI lower bound 0.00), -0.06% when the lead cycle is not credited; the full corpus reaches 0.89-1.62% only with the older $0.36 fixed cost per block, and its context guard fails (33% of merged 16-blocks predicted over 60k, limit 10%). Few plans exceed 8 tasks and the run-unit intercept fell to about $0.02 after 10-09. Only the block-merge route of wake coalescing is covered; wake coalescing itself stays unproven. $0 spent. Evidence: [2026-10-20-block-cap-16.md](results/2026-10-20-block-cap-16.md).

metric: Saving, % of build-task cost

measured: Status: rejected. The gate's 5% bucket estimate was 2.9 times too high (carry priced at $0.30 per M instead of the model that ran, Sonnet cacheRead $0.10 per M). The bar reads as a pass against the carry bucket alone (60.8%), but that bucket is 1.73% of build-task cost, and the 20% fallback share is assumed, not measured; at a 60% fallback the flagged-agent saving drops to 2.01%. The quality guard passes (1 of 56). The tester returned BLOCKED on the reading; the lead ruled FAIL on the gate's wording. $0 spent. Evidence: [2026-10-20-build-task-range-reads.md](results/2026-10-20-build-task-range-reads.md).
retryWhen: a real-use A/B measures how much a build-task re-reads after a range read, or whole-file reads over 8k chars grow past 3% of build-task cost.

mechanism: (`build-task` diagnoses after its 2nd red Proof run and returns BLOCKED when the plan is the cause, instead of looping).
metric: Net saving, % of build-task cost
threshold: CI lower bound at least 3% of build-task cost
measured: Status: rejected. Replay of 508 real-use build-tasks ($78.06): 85 agents loop (at least 2 red runs, $22.73, 29% of cost). The quality guard passes (plan-defect share 41%, green within one more edit 35%) but the saving does not. $0 spent. Evidence: [2026-10-20-red-loop-breaker.md](results/2026-10-20-red-loop-breaker.md).

measured: Status: rejected. Hash-equal re-reads are at most 1.56% of repair cost and 0.172% of run [0.11, 0.24]; realizable 0.88% of repair cost [0.65, 1.19] and 0.097% of run (n=122 runs, 264 repair dispatches), missed by about 15x; 13.9% of matched repairs edit a matched path. mechanism: (when a landed-gate failure returns to a task, resume that `build-task` by agent id with `SendMessage` so it keeps its file reads).
metric: Saving, % of run cost (carry-model replay)
threshold: at least 3% of the post-GREEN repair bucket and 0.3% of run, with a CI lower bound above 0
measured: Status: rejected. Tested as: run-unit runs `land-task --check` after GREEN and resumes the same builder with `SendMessage` on a refusal. Earlier path-level overlap: 239 of 264 repairs (90.5%) read a path an earlier attempt read, 2.2% of run [1.5, 2.9] and 20.2% of repair cost (n=122 runs), which includes re-reads after edits, so a resume saving was not shown ([2026-10-20-repair-inherits-facts.md](results/2026-10-20-repair-inherits-facts.md)). $0 spent. Evidence: [2026-10-20-resume-builder-on-refusal.md](results/2026-10-20-resume-builder-on-refusal.md); source: confidence low (one source): [SDK subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents) (resume keeps the full history).

measured: Status: partial. $0.120/cell, 8.8% under main ($0.132) but 8% above the cheapest rival ($0.1107); hidden tests 19/25 (5,5,4,0,5), ties the best rival; 0 question-ending cells; test-pollution 0/5. Quality bar met, cost bar missed.

title: Round 2 bundle: dispatch rules at first Agent call, compression opt-in, short agent descriptions, done-rule lines (T3)
mechanism: Move dispatch rules to the first Agent call (A), make session-text compression opt-in (B), shorten agent descriptions (C) and add variant and warning done-rule lines (F), tested together as T3.
metric: USD per cell and hidden tests, n=5 x 5 tasks, sonnet
threshold: USD/cell under the cheapest rival, hidden tests above 19/25, no task 2 or more below round 1
measured: Status: rejected, superseded by round 3. $0.1575/cell against $0.1126 for the cheapest rival in the same batch (+40%; round 1 was $0.1203); hidden tests 20/25; add-field-migration 3/5 against 5/5 in round 1, so the task bar failed too. First-call cache write fell only 482 tokens (5,828 against 6,310), not the expected 1,200. The rise came from per-turn work, not standing text: the done-rule lines (F) cause about 80% of it through longer variant-proof loops, more README reads and more test code.
retryWhen: the done-rule lines are bounded (see round 3) and the standing-text cuts are tested on their own.

title: Round 3 bundle: bounded proof (one run per variant), proof reuse (T4)
mechanism: Round 2 with the variant done-rule bounded to one run per named variant, no repeat loops, and an earlier proof reused instead of rerun (G).
metric: USD per cell and hidden tests, n=5 x 5 tasks, sonnet
threshold: USD/cell under the cheapest rival, hidden tests above 19/25, no task 2 or more below round 2
measured: Status: landed for quality, cost bar missed. $0.1496/cell (round 2 $0.1575, round 1 $0.1203) against $0.1090 for the cheapest rival (+37%); hidden tests 22/25 (5,5,5,2,5) against 17/25 for that rival; no task below round 2; 50/50 cells, 0 api_error. First-call cache write 5,801 tokens, about 770 above the rival. Output tokens per cell 4,056 against 2,718. A 4-cell smoke run first cost $0.1546 (add-field) and $0.1006 (test-pollution).
retryWhen: tool output, test code and report length are cut toward the cheapest rival without losing the 22/25.

title: Run the wave loop in a `Workflow` script
mechanism: (the `Workflow` tool orchestrates fan-out, wait and land in a script outside the conversation, so lead turns between slots disappear).
measured: Status: untried. It could cut lead turns per wave (poll, dispatch, land) and lead context, but it is a TypeScript SDK feature whose availability inside exo's plugin and fit to `Parallel:` waves are unverified, and it must keep the `land-slot` gates. Nearest entry: script-owned fan-out (`next-task --slots`), which stays inside the lead's turns. No Anthropic-engineer talk transcript was found; the only talk summary read is third-party ([dev.to](https://dev.to/kazuya_dev/aws-reinvent-2025-what-anthropic-learned-building-ai-agents-in-2025-aim277-16lc)) and it says sub-agents "didn't parallelize well in practice", so the claim below rests on docs and blog posts, not a talk. Evidence: unmeasured, confidence low: [SDK subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents) ("scale up with dynamic workflows"), [best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices).
retryWhen: the script-owned fan-out has been measured and lead turns between slots show as the critical path, and `Workflow` is confirmed usable from a plugin.

title: `run-unit` at `low` effort on the balanced profile
measured: Status: landed-but-no-gain. It applied in 2 of 3 candidate runs, run-unit wall fell 25-34% with overlapping ranges, and total wall, cost and tokens show no supported effect. Evidence: [2026-10-19-build-speed-rerun.md](results/2026-10-19-build-speed-rerun.md).
retryWhen: a rerun with the effort applied in every run, and the review stages held equal across arms, shows a total effect.

title: run-unit cache TTL back to 5 minutes
mechanism: Delete `experimental: { cacheTtl: 1h }` in `agents/run-unit.md`.
measured: Status: rejected. Sweep cells looked cheaper ($11.42 to $7.14, 167 agents, 0 gaps over 300 s), but real use cost +58% ($5.21 to $8.26, 442 agents, 215 of 11,166 gaps over 300 s). Sweep cells never idle 5 minutes, so TTL ideas need real-use transcripts. Evidence: [2026-10-20-cache-ttl-real-use.md](results/2026-10-20-cache-ttl-real-use.md).
retryWhen: real-use run-unit gaps over 300 s become rare.

title: run-unit hands over at a context line, not by task count
mechanism: (`run-unit` returns a HANDOVER line after a landing once its context passes 50k tokens, and the lead dispatches a fresh unit).
metric: Net saving, % of run-unit cost
threshold: CI lower bound at least 3% of run-unit cost
measured: Status: rejected. Replay of 98 real-use run-units in 49 sessions ($28.10): 19 cross 50k, 11 can split. Net saving -3.79% of run-unit cost [-6.14, -0.63] with the measured $0.097 lead cycle; +0.02% [-1.34, 2.44] with a free lead cycle. 40k, 60k and repeat-split variants all stay under +1%. The quality guard fails: 2 of 11 split units (18%, limit 10%) message a pre-split build, and 8 of 11 have a build in flight at the split. $0 spent. Evidence: [2026-10-20-run-unit-context-handover.md](results/2026-10-20-run-unit-context-handover.md).
retryWhen: run-units regularly pass 100k early in a block, so the carry per request outweighs about $0.19 for a fresh startup plus a lead cycle.

title: Script-owned fan-out (`next-task.mjs --slots`)
measured: Status: no gain, slower at n=15. Wall +47.2 s (+24.8% mean, CI [+12.2, +83.9] s, exact MW p=0.037), cost +2.7% (within noise), hidden 17/17 in both arms. Round 2's -12% at n=5 did not replicate. Evidence: [2026-10-19-speed-round3.md](results/2026-10-19-speed-round3.md), earlier [2026-10-19-speed-round2.md](results/2026-10-19-speed-round2.md).
retryWhen: the wave or slot setup changes so that run-unit's own worktree creation is the measured bottleneck; the code is in [2026-10-19-speed-round3.md](results/2026-10-19-speed-round3.md).

title: Script stdout contract: a few lines by default, one `ERROR <reason>` line per failure, detail to a `.exo/*.log`, `--verbose` for the rest
mechanism: (stays under the 25k-token tool-output cap so nothing spills to `<persisted-output>`; `npm run check` could lint it).
measured: Status: untried. It saves a little wall time (fewer spill detours, shorter reads) and input tokens, but it is a repo-wide rule where the "one review bundle" entry covers one file, and no wall figure exists. Evidence: unmeasured, confidence medium-low (principle agreed, no wall figure): [building a C compiler](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-c-compiler), [writing tools for agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents) (concise format 72 vs 206 tokens).
retryWhen: tool outputs of exo scripts keep spilling or long outputs show as a measured share of input tokens.

title: Script-written build report: `land-task.mjs --check --compose`
mechanism: (the model states landed clause, Red and test-first; the script runs Proof, writes the `.diff`, `.log` and report block).
measured: Status: untried. It saves 20-35 s over four tasks and removes report-format retries, but it overlaps with candidate 3 above and must land as its output-side superset or after it. Evidence: unmeasured (transcript estimate).
retryWhen: candidate 3 has landed, or build-task report turns show as a measured share of its wall time.

title: Scripted acceptance of the fix diff replaces the second `review-branch`
mechanism: (`run-probes.mjs --scope`: the fix touches only files named by `fix` findings, drops no test or assertion, adds no skip marker, stays under a size cap).
measured: Status: untried. It saves about 13 s per run and one review dispatch, but the probe proves the finding fixed, not that the fix adds no new defect. Evidence: unmeasured (transcript estimate).
retryWhen: a run with a `fix` finding shows the second review adding no finding on the fix diff across several runs.

title: Scripts print the next step
mechanism: `next-task.mjs` prints the filled prompt and opens a wave's slots; `verify.mjs --reviews-only` and `merge-reviews.mjs` print the DISPATCH and FINDING lines.
measured: Status: landed. Flow-unit n=15: wall -22.4% (p=0.026), cost -15.6% (p=0.0023), tokens -14.3%, run-unit calls -4.4, lead calls -3.7, hidden 255/255 in both arms. Most of the wall gap follows a 6-v-1 fix-loop imbalance (Fisher p=0.080); stage-matched wall -5.6% (p=0.52), latency-normalized -21.0 s (p=0.0012); the arm's own gain is likely 5-10%. Evidence: [round 6](results/2026-10-19-speed-round6.md).

title: Session-text compression opt-in (B)
mechanism: Drop the default report clamp so session text is no longer compressed unless asked.
metric: USD per cell and hidden tests, n=5 x 5 tasks, sonnet
threshold: net cost per cell below round 1
measured: Status: rejected, no gain. Attribution from the round 2 transcripts: visible text rose from 1,230 to 1,800 chars per cell (about +$0.003) while the removed clamp text saved about $0.0022, so net about $0 to +$0.001. exo then wrote more than the cheapest rival (1,543 chars).
retryWhen: a one-line report clamp is restored and measured on its own.

title: Short verbs: a `bin/exo-step` command (`next`, `land 3`, `wait 2,3`, `check 3`) reading plan and root from `.exo/run.json`
measured: Status: untried. It saves 30-35 s per run in about 2.2k fewer output tokens, but plan and root can resolve wrongly in a slot worktree and it touches prompt lines in 4-5 files. Evidence: unmeasured (transcript estimate).
retryWhen: the harness puts plugin `bin/` on PATH, or lead and run-unit command lines show as a measured share of output tokens.

title: Skip `wait-report` after a foreground `Next:` build
measured: Status: landed-but-no-gain. Run-unit never called `wait-report` after a foreground build in either arm, so the rule changed no behavior. Evidence: [2026-10-19-build-speed-rerun.md](results/2026-10-19-build-speed-rerun.md).
retryWhen: a run shows `run-unit` waiting on a foreground build.

title: Spec stops at path level and the builder reads the lines
mechanism: (in spec the lead verifies only that a path and symbol exist, names them in the task, and leaves line-level reading to the builder, which reads them anyway).
metric: Duplicated lead line reads, % of the spec code-read bucket
threshold: at least 30% of the bucket as a point estimate, with a CI lower bound above 3% of it
measured: Status: rejected. Of the lead code line reads in 25 post-10-09 spec windows ($5.02, 2.79% of run), 17.3% [9.5, 25.0] are paths a builder reads later, 0.48% of run [0.21, 0.86]; the point estimate and the upper bound miss 30%. Repair-rate guard underpowered (25 repair dispatches, gap -6.7 points). Almost all windows are exo-repo use; cross-session joins not made. $0 spent. Evidence: [2026-10-20-spec-path-level.md](results/2026-10-20-spec-path-level.md).
retryWhen: a larger spec corpus outside the exo repo shows over 30% of lead line reads duplicated by the builder, with the repair-rate gap under 5 points.

title: Speculative next-action execution
measured: Status: rejected. One paper, outside coding, and cost goes up. Evidence: unmeasured.
retryWhen: a coding-task result shows a wall-time gain at flat cost.

title: Speculative pathfinder: fan out the wave with Task 1 and hold landings until it lands
mechanism: (`land-slot.mjs` refuses `HOLD` while the pathfinder is unlanded).
measured: Status: untried. It saves about 25-30 s on runs with a ready wave at start, but a failing or drifting Task 1 wastes up to three builds (about 11-15k tokens each). Evidence: unmeasured (transcript estimate).
retryWhen: the script-owned fan-out has landed and a run shows the Task 1 alone phase on the critical path.

title: Stall hedging (cancel and resend a stalled request)
mechanism: Cancel a request that runs more than about 3x its predicted latency and send it again.
measured: Status: untried. Stalled requests are 25% of within-class wall variance (37.5% at a 5 s threshold): 1.0% of requests, 0.6 per run on the critical path, mean 8.9 s, sd 17.2 s, sonnet only (0 of 507 opus requests). Hedging would remove most of the 8.9 s mean stall time per run. exo cannot do it: it needs Claude Code harness or API support. Evidence: [round 6, Cause of the spread](results/2026-10-19-speed-round6.md), 75 runs from rounds 3 to 5.
retryWhen: Claude Code or the API exposes a request timeout with resend, or per-request cancel.

title: Start reviews without waiting for the gate
mechanism: (`verify.mjs --reviews-only` runs in the foreground, then the full gate runs in the background in the same message as the review dispatch).
measured: Landed in 779e1294 (2026-10-10); `skills/verify/SKILL.md` step 1 carries it. The foreground gate wait falls to about 0.6 s per verify. Round 6 re-proposed it (L1.3) and the $0 check found it already landed: of 25 post-change verify.mjs --plan calls only 1 was a foreground `--reviews-only` call, and the 11 foreground full gates (sum 778 s) predate or straddle the change. Evidence: [2026-10-20-verify-reviews-first.md](results/2026-10-20-verify-reviews-first.md).

title: The dispatch carries the read set
mechanism: (`next-task.mjs` prints a filled `implementer-prompt.md` block with the brief, `run-rules.md` and `lean.md` inlined, so `build-task` and `run-unit` skip their reads).
measured: Status: untried. It saves 10-20 s per run (3 turns per build-task, 2 per run-unit dispatch round), but the prompt grows and the brief is no longer read from its file. Evidence: unmeasured (transcript estimate).
retryWhen: a run shows the brief and rules reads as a measured share of build-task wall time.

title: `thinking: between_tools` for mechanical agents
mechanism: (Sonnet 5.5; drop up-front thinking for `run-unit` and `fix-review`, only if Claude Code exposes it per agent).
measured: Status: untried. It could cut wall time per turn, but routing risk is the reason a cheaper `run-unit` was rejected, and the ledger tested effort levels, not the thinking mode. Evidence: unmeasured, confidence low (one source, no per-agent control found): [effort](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort).
retryWhen: Claude Code exposes the thinking mode per agent and `run-unit` holds its routing pressure cases with it.

title: Trim passing runner output to its tail
mechanism: A passing test, build or check run by an agent leaves only its last 20 lines in context; a failing run stays in full.
measured: Status: rejected. Net saving share (95% bootstrap CI) against a 3% bar: build-task 0.14% [0.11, 0.17] (n=1,939), solve-hard 0.09% [0.04, 0.14] (n=201), run-unit 0.02% [0.01, 0.04] (n=315), lead 0.02% [0.02, 0.03] (n=1,017). Agents already pipe or redirect 81% of runner calls (6,127 of 7,577), and later turns quoted a cut line in 6.4% of trimmed results. Evidence: [2026-10-20-bash-trim.md](results/2026-10-20-bash-trim.md).
retryWhen: agents stop piping or redirecting runner output (for example a headless prompt that streams it), or passing runner output shows as a measured share of input tokens.

title: Verdict-first review output with a finding cap and a `--diff-only` scope for the fix-diff review
mechanism: (`review-branch.md` writes `VERDICT`, then at most N finding lines, no "checked, fine" prose).
measured: Status: untried. It saves 12-25 s per run, but less thinking aloud may miss defects, the highest quality risk of the verify ideas. Evidence: unmeasured (transcript estimate).
retryWhen: a seeded-defect fixture shows the catch rate unchanged with the shorter output.

title: Verify in a fresh subagent
mechanism: (build `tail.md` step 7 dispatches `verify` to one fresh subagent and the lead keeps at most 5 lines plus a REPORT path).
metric: Saving, % of run cost
threshold: at least 1.5% of run cost and 3% of the verify window
measured: Status: rejected. Saving is 10.17% of the lead verify window [4.52, 15.33] but 1.43% of run cost [0.63, 2.23], under the 1.5% bar (n=93 runs); it flips to -0.58% [-1.53, 0.28] at a 20k fresh context and no agent with Skill and a 1h cache exists. $0 spent. Evidence: [2026-10-20-verify-subagent.md](results/2026-10-20-verify-subagent.md).
retryWhen: a measured subagent fresh context is under 8k tokens, or an existing agent can run `exo:verify` on a 1h cache.

title: `verify.mjs` runs the reviewer's mechanical rules
mechanism: (the `Red:` grep, test-first per task, deleted tests, removed assertions and skip markers become `defect` lines merged by `merge-reviews.mjs`).
measured: Status: untried. It saves 10-20 s per run of reviewer round trips and cannot be skipped by a model, but a regex can miss a test runner it does not know. Evidence: unmeasured (transcript estimate).
retryWhen: review-branch tool calls on the `Red:` and skip-marker checks show as a measured share of verify wall time.

title: Verify scripts print the chained next step
mechanism: (`verify.mjs` and `merge-reviews.mjs` print the chained next step, so the lead acts once per stage and reads fewer report files).
metric: Removable share of the lead runner bucket
threshold: bootstrap 95% CI lower bound at least 3% of the runner bucket, at least 15 sessions
measured: Status: rejected. Estimate 2.37% of the bucket, CI [1.63, 3.20]; the full removable class is 4.74% [3.29, 6.41] but is an unsupported upper bound. Only 11 current-design sessions have a review phase (floor 15). The lead runs verify.mjs or merge-reviews in 10 of 325 verify-phase requests; the largest class is reading report and background-task output, which is waiting on the gate. $0 spent, paid step not run. Evidence: [2026-10-20-verify-lead-turn-floor.md](results/2026-10-20-verify-lead-turn-floor.md).
retryWhen: at least 15 current-design sessions with a review phase show script-run requests or report rereads as a measured share of the lead bucket above 6%.

title: Benchmark cells let git refresh its xcrun cache
mechanism: Benchmark cells under the macOS sandbox let git refresh its xcrun cache.
measured: Each git call no longer costs about 0.4 s, `CHANGELOG.md`.
